author: claude-fable-5-2
theme: One ordinary week on a mid-market customer success desk, where the CRM, the rep's typed notes, the recorded call, and the later Slack thread each give a slightly different seat count, price, date, or stage for the same account.

accounts.name: Kestrel Ridge Mechanical
accounts.risk_reason: Denver branch (38 seats) says it will move to Corvane unless offline sync bug FD-4630 is fixed and verified by 2027-02-01. CFO will sign one year and run an RFP in the fall unless multi-year price protection lands. A 46-to-60 seat expansion (Brannock Air acquisition) is in flight at the same time.

opportunities.name: Kestrel Ridge - Brannock Air expansion (60 tech seats)

call_notes.body: QBR w/ Renata + Fiona. Usage good: 131/140 tech seats active wkly, 12/12 dispatch. Renata mentioned a 'possible acquisition' in Q4, wouldnt name the co. Fiona: route optimizer ignoring lunch windows for the Tulsa crew, logged FD-4471. AI: Priya send adoption report by 9/22. AI: Sam O look at 4471 by 9/24.

Renata confirmed the acquisiton = Brannock Air (Colorado Springs), closes Dec 1. ~60 techs, 5 dispatchers, currently on paper + a spreadsheeet. Wants them on Fennick by March. Asked abt volume pricing over 200 seats. Said I'd bring Tobias. Did NOT quote.

Luis B (Denver) escalation. Offline sync on Android dropped 3 completed work orders last wk, techs re-entered by hand. 2nd time since Aug he says. 'If this happens in January I'm done.' He has ALREADY had a Corvane demo (!!) and Renata doesn't know. Ticket FD-4630, P2. AI: Priya get eng ETA by 11/10. AI: Priya tell Renata? asking Lena first.
Voicemail.

Renewal kickoff, Renata + Noor (procurement) + Tobias. Noor: any deal >$100k/yr needs 3 quotes OR a multi-year w/ price protection, CFO's rule since Oct. Desmond wants 3 yrs, flat price, 8% off. Tobias floated 3yr @ $58/tech seat w/ 4% cap on yr 2/3 uplift. Noor: 'a cap is not flat.' Dispatcher price not discussed at all. AI: Tobias written proposal by 12/10. AI: Noor send vendor form by 12/8 (not received as of 12/15).

Gareth (IT). SSO cutover to their new IdP planned for the Jan 23-24 weekend. Needs SCIM for the Brannock users, we only have SCIM on Enterprise tier. He assumed it was included. It is not in Tobias's proposal. Flagged to Tobias. Also Gareth says Brannock headcount is 'more like 45 real employees, the rest are subs' which conflicts w/ the 60 in the opp.

Renewal call (recorded). Desmond pushed hard: 3 yrs flat or he signs 1 yr and runs an RFP in the fall. Luis on for 10 min, Denver stays ONLY if 4630 is fixed and he's seen it work by 2/1. Brannock seats stated as 60 on the call. Tobias verbally offered $58 flat yr 1-2, +3% yr 3. Desmond: 'send it, I'll look.' No commitment.
AI: Tobias revised order form by Thu 1/14.
AI: Priya eng written commit on FD-4630 by 1/15.
AI: Renata final Brannock seat list by Fri 1/15.

Quick call w Renata, 8 min. Seat list coming tmrw, she thinks 46 not 60. Desmond 'cooled off' after seeing $58 in writing, but she says he'll go after dispatcher seats next, those were never discounted ($110). She will NOT be on the 1/20 call (jury duty), Fiona covering. Fiona has no signing authority.

slack_messages.author: Priya Nandakumar
slack_messages.body: Luis at Kestrel Denver has already sat through a Corvane demo. Renata doesn't know. 38 seats in that branch, ~$28k. Do I tell her?

slack_messages.author: Lena Brzezinski
slack_messages.body: Yes, but tell Luis first that you're going to. Don't blindside him, he's the one living with the sync bug.

slack_messages.author: Tobias Wren
slack_messages.body: Proposal out to Noor + Desmond. 3yr, 200 tech seats @ $58, 4% cap on years 2 and 3. TCV $417,600.

slack_messages.author: Anneke Vos
slack_messages.body: @Tobias $58 on 200 seats isn't approved. Floor at that volume on a 3yr is $59.50. $58 needs Lena plus VP sign-off and I have neither on file. Also your TCV leaves out the 12 dispatcher seats, so the number is wrong twice.

slack_messages.author: Tobias Wren
slack_messages.body: Dispatcher seats sit in the base renewal opp, not the expansion, so the TCV is right for what it covers. Fair on the floor. I'll get the sign-off.

slack_messages.author: Priya Nandakumar
slack_messages.body: Call done. Desmond wants flat for 3 years. Brannock = 60 seats. Denver conditional on FD-4630 by 2/1. Notes in SF.

slack_messages.author: Priya Nandakumar
slack_messages.body: Correction to my 1/12 message: Brannock is 46 seats, not 60. 14 are subcontractors who won't get logins. Renata confirmed today. Expansion opp is overstated by 14 seats, about $9.7k/yr at $58.

slack_messages.author: Hugo Tran
slack_messages.body: So total tech seats = 186, under the 200 tier. $58 was priced on 200. Someone has to tell Desmond the per-seat goes UP when the count goes down. Not it.

slack_messages.author: Sam Oyelaran
slack_messages.body: FD-4630: fix is in mobile 8.14, store review pending. Eng will NOT commit in writing to 2/1. Best they'll say is 'targeting the week of 1/25'. Sorry Priya.

slack_messages.author: Lena Brzezinski
slack_messages.body: ack

transcript.text:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:01.200 --> 00:00:05.640
Tobias Wren: Okay, recording's on. Um, Desmond, thanks for making the time.

2
00:00:06.010 --> 00:00:10.320
Desmond Achebe: Sure. I've got a hard stop at half past, so let's just get into it.

3
00:00:10.900 --> 00:00:17.450
Tobias Wren: Yep. So, uh, the proposal from December tenth. Three years, fifty-eight a seat on the technician side, and then the—

4
00:00:17.100 --> 00:00:21.800
Desmond Achebe: With a four percent cap. Which is not what I asked for. I asked for flat.

5
00:00:22.050 --> 00:00:26.300
Tobias Wren: Right, and I, I hear that. The cap is a ceiling, it's not a—

6
00:00:25.700 --> 00:00:29.900
Desmond Achebe: It's a ceiling you will hit. Every vendor hits the ceiling.

7
00:00:30.400 --> 00:00:41.150
Renata Kowalczyk: Can I, sorry, can I jump in? Desmond, the per-seat today is sixty-two. So fifty-eight is already, what, six, six and a half percent down.

8
00:00:41.600 --> 00:00:42.900
Desmond Achebe: I asked for eight.

9
00:00:43.800 --> 00:00:52.200
Priya Nandakumar: And the, um, the volume is part of how we got there. That's with Brannock, the sixty seats, getting you to two hundred.

10
00:00:52.600 --> 00:00:56.000
Renata Kowalczyk: Sixty-ish. I still owe you the real list.

11
00:00:57.300 --> 00:01:02.100
Luis Barrientos: Hey, sorry, I'm late, I was on a roof. Can you all hear me?

12
00:01:02.500 --> 00:01:04.200
Priya Nandakumar: We can hear you, Luis. Hi.

13
00:01:04.900 --> 00:01:19.700
Luis Barrientos: So I'll be quick 'cause I gotta get back up there. Denver. We lost work orders again in November. Three of them. My guys don't trust the app offline anymore, they're taking pictures of paper again.

14
00:01:20.300 --> 00:01:27.050
Priya Nandakumar: Yeah. And that's, that's FD-4630, engineering has a fix going into the next mobile release, so—

15
00:01:26.400 --> 00:01:27.100
Luis Barrientos: When?

16
00:01:27.900 --> 00:01:34.600
Priya Nandakumar: I'm getting a written date this week. I don't want to give you a date I made up.

17
00:01:35.200 --> 00:01:49.800
Luis Barrientos: Okay. I appreciate that. But here's mine. February first. If it's not fixed, and I haven't seen it work on my own guys' phones by February first, I'm asking Renata to let Denver go to the other thing.

18
00:01:50.300 --> 00:01:51.500
Desmond Achebe: What other thing?

19
00:01:52.400 --> 00:02:01.000
Renata Kowalczyk: Corvane. Luis had a demo. I found out in November. From Priya, actually.

20
00:02:01.700 --> 00:02:09.300
Desmond Achebe: So we'd be running two systems. No. No, that's, that's not happening. Luis, we'll talk offline.

21
00:02:09.800 --> 00:02:12.400
Luis Barrientos: Fine by me. I gotta drop. Thanks, all.

22
00:02:14.000 --> 00:02:29.500
Tobias Wren: So, um, Desmond, on the flat piece. What I can do, and I'd need to confirm it internally, is fifty-eight flat for years one and two, and three percent in year three. Not a cap. Just three.

23
00:02:30.100 --> 00:02:31.900
Desmond Achebe: And if I say one year?

24
00:02:32.600 --> 00:02:39.800
Tobias Wren: One year is, uh, it's sixty-two, same as today. There's no volume break without the term.

25
00:02:40.300 --> 00:02:53.100
Desmond Achebe: Then I sign one year and I run an RFP in the fall. I'm not threatening you, that's just the policy. Over a hundred K it's three quotes or a multi-year with protection.

26
00:02:53.000 --> 00:02:54.600
Renata Kowalczyk: Which is why we're—

27
00:02:54.200 --> 00:03:02.700
Desmond Achebe: I know why we're here. Send it. Fifty-eight, fifty-eight, plus three. I'll look. I'm not saying yes.

28
00:03:03.300 --> 00:03:05.900
Tobias Wren: Understood. You'll have it Thursday.

29
00:03:06.400 --> 00:03:09.800
Renata Kowalczyk: And I'll get Priya the Brannock list by Friday.

30
00:03:10.200 --> 00:03:12.500
Desmond Achebe: Okay. I have to go. Thank you.

accounts.name: Pelham & Oster Plumbing
accounts.risk_reason: Champion Carla Menendez left on 2026-11-20. The GM now deciding had never seen the invoice. Contract lapsed 2026-12-31; tenant is in grace until 2027-01-30, then read-only. 31 of 45 seats active.

call_notes.body: Carla: renewal is 'a formality', same 45 seats, wants the PO done by Thanksgiving. Moved opp to Verbal Commit.

Carla's cell is disconnected. Email bounced 12/1. Trish (office mgr) picked up the main line: Carla's last day was 11/20, 'went to a competitor of ours, not yours.' Wendell decides everything now. Trish doesn't know what Fennick costs or who signs. AI: Dale intro email to Wendell today.

Call w/ Wendell + Trish (Otter recording attached). Not hostile, just doesn't know why he's paying $35k. Thinks they have 30 plumbers not 45. Wants usage by person. Asked for month to month, we dont have that. Told him grace ends 1/30 then read-only. AI: Dale usage export by Fri 1/8 (he said the ninth on the call, Friday is the 8th). AI: Wendell answer by 1/22.

slack_messages.author: Dale Okafor
slack_messages.body: Pelham & Oster: Carla Menendez is gone as of 11/20. Opp says Verbal Commit. That commit left the building with her. Marking at_risk.

slack_messages.author: Hugo Tran
slack_messages.body: Stage is still Verbal Commit in SF and forecast call is tomorrow. Are you fixing it or am I?

slack_messages.author: Dale Okafor
slack_messages.body: you

slack_messages.author: Dale Okafor
slack_messages.body: Usage export sent to Wendell and Trish. 31 of 45 seats logged in during the last 90 days. He guessed 30. So he's right, and the renewal at 45 is dead. Realistic is 31 to 33 seats, $24,180 to $25,740. Also the stage STILL says Verbal Commit.

slack_messages.author: Lena Brzezinski
slack_messages.body: Offer 33 at $65 with a true-up clause. Don't discount the seat price on top of a seat cut.

accounts.name: Marlowe County Water Authority
accounts.risk_reason: County procurement freeze since 2026-12-14: no purchase order can be issued for anything but payroll and emergency repair. Customer wants to renew. Contract ends today; a no-cost bridge to 2027-04-15 was signed this morning.

call_notes.body: Howard (purchasing): county board froze all non-payroll POs on 12/14 pending an audit of the general fund. No end date. 'Could be Feb, could be the new fiscal yr in July.' Our renewal PO was 2 signatures from done. Ingrid furious, not at us.

Teams call Ingrid + Howard + Tobias (recorded). Options we brought: (a) no-cost extension, (b) invoice now on net-120, (c) let it lapse. Howard can't take (b): an invoice w/o a PO is an 'unauthorized commitment' and he personally gets written up. Ingrid wants (a). Tobias said 60 days, would try for 90. AI: Tobias extension letter by Wed 1/13. AI: Howard send the freeze memo by 1/12 (received 1/12, in the opp).

Howard called ME, which never happens. Board meets 1/26, there is now an exemption list w/ 'critical operations software' on it and we are item 14 of 31. If exempted, PO roughly 10 business days later, so earliest ~2/9. He wants the extension letter dated before 1/15 so the auditors see no gap in coverage.

slack_messages.author: Tobias Wren
slack_messages.body: MCWA needs a no-cost bridge, county PO freeze. I told them 60 days on the call.

slack_messages.author: Anneke Vos
slack_messages.body: 60 is fine. For what it's worth policy lets me approve up to 90 for public sector when there's a freeze memo on file. Get the memo.

slack_messages.author: Tobias Wren
slack_messages.body: Memo's attached to the opp. Going with 90 not 60 since Anneke can approve it, new end date 4/15. Ingrid already told her crew chiefs 60 so somebody please correct that with her.

slack_messages.author: Marit Solheim
slack_messages.body: MCWA extension letter countersigned 9:02 this morning, dated 1/14. Opp close date still says today, moving it to 2/26. Hugo please don't flag this as slipped, it's a freeze, not a slip.

transcript.text:
WEBVTT

00:00:03.120 --> 00:00:08.450
<v Marit Solheim>Hi Ingrid, hi Howard. Tobias is joining, he's, um, he's just getting off another call.</v>

00:00:08.900 --> 00:00:11.200
<v Ingrid Vasquez-Bell>That's fine. Howard, you're on mute.</v>

00:00:14.050 --> 00:00:16.700
<v Howard Lim>Sorry. Yes. Can you hear me now?</v>

00:00:16.900 --> 00:00:18.100
<v Marit Solheim>Yep, we've got you.</v>

00:00:21.300 --> 00:00:24.600
<v Tobias Wren>Hey, sorry, sorry everyone. Tobias here.</v>

00:00:25.100 --> 00:00:38.900
<v Ingrid Vasquez-Bell>So I'll start. We want to renew. Nothing has changed about that. I have eighty people in the field on this every day and I am not going back to radios and clipboards.</v>

00:00:39.400 --> 00:00:51.200
<v Howard Lim>And I have a memo from the county administrator dated December fourteenth that says I cannot issue a purchase order for anything that isn't payroll or an emergency repair.</v>

00:00:51.800 --> 00:00:57.300
<v Tobias Wren>Understood. So, um, we talked internally and there's a few ways we could—</v>

00:00:56.700 --> 00:01:00.900
<v Howard Lim>Before you list them. I can't accept an invoice either.</v>

00:01:01.400 --> 00:01:06.800
<v Tobias Wren>Even at, like, net one-twenty? So it wouldn't actually be due until—</v>

00:01:07.100 --> 00:01:16.500
<v Howard Lim>It's not about when it's due. An invoice without a P.O. is an unauthorized commitment. That's my name on it. I'd get written up.</v>

00:01:16.900 --> 00:01:19.800
<v Ingrid Vasquez-Bell>He would. It happened to someone in Parks.</v>

00:01:20.600 --> 00:01:36.200
<v Tobias Wren>Okay. Okay, that's, that's helpful. So that takes B off the table. Then it's really an extension. We keep you live, no charge, for a set period, and the renewal term starts when the P.O. lands.</v>

00:01:36.700 --> 00:01:37.600
<v Ingrid Vasquez-Bell>How long?</v>

00:01:38.200 --> 00:01:42.900
<v Tobias Wren>I can do sixty days today. Ninety I'd have to—</v>

00:01:42.300 --> 00:01:47.800
<v Marit Solheim>Sorry, Tobias, I think for public sector there's a, isn't there a longer—</v>

00:01:47.200 --> 00:01:56.400
<v Tobias Wren>There might be. I don't want to promise ninety on this call and then walk it back. Sixty I can say yes to right now.</v>

00:01:57.000 --> 00:02:03.500
<v Ingrid Vasquez-Bell>Sixty gets me to mid-March. Howard, is the freeze over by mid-March?</v>

00:02:04.100 --> 00:02:14.700
<v Howard Lim>I don't know. Nobody knows. The audit's on the general fund. Could be February. Could be July, with the new fiscal year.</v>

00:02:15.300 --> 00:02:16.000
<v Ingrid Vasquez-Bell>July.</v>

00:02:16.600 --> 00:02:18.400
<v Howard Lim>I'm telling you what I know.</v>

00:02:19.500 --> 00:02:25.100
<v Marit Solheim>Howard, is there, um, an exemption process? Some counties keep a list.</v>

00:02:25.800 --> 00:02:35.300
<v Howard Lim>There's talk of one. The board meets on the twenty-sixth. I can ask whether software for field crews would count.</v>

00:02:35.900 --> 00:02:39.200
<v Ingrid Vasquez-Bell>It's how we find the valves, Howard. It counts.</v>

00:02:40.100 --> 00:02:56.800
<v Tobias Wren>So here's what I'll do. Extension letter, sixty days minimum, I'll try for ninety, to you by Wednesday the thirteenth. And Howard, could you send over the freeze memo? Our finance people will want it on file.</v>

00:02:57.300 --> 00:03:01.000
<v Howard Lim>I can send it tomorrow. It's a public document.</v>

00:03:01.600 --> 00:03:04.200
<v Ingrid Vasquez-Bell>And the price doesn't move while we wait.</v>

00:03:04.800 --> 00:03:09.500
<v Tobias Wren>Price doesn't move. Eighty seats at sixty, same as the quote.</v>

00:03:10.100 --> 00:03:15.700
<v Ingrid Vasquez-Bell>Good. Then we're fine. I mean, we're not fine, but we're fine with you.</v>

accounts.name: Dunmore Elevator Services
accounts.risk_reason: Formal evaluation of Corvane since November; decision at their board on 2027-02-19. Started as a compliance-reporting gap, became a price comparison once the controller joined ($54 base at Corvane vs our $64).

call_notes.body: Aoife told me straight: they're evaluating Corvane, started in Nov. Not a secret, 'I'd rather you hear it from me.' Driver = Marcus's state inspection reporting. He exports to CSV and rebuilds the certificate log in Excel every month, ~2 days of his time. Corvane showed him a built-in inspection log. Price not raised once. AI: Marit get Sam to scope whether our compliance pack covers state form EL-7 by 12/16.

Sam demoed the compliance pack to Marcus. Covers certificate log + overdue alerts. Does NOT produce the EL-7 PDF, Marcus still fills the form, but from one screen instead of an export. Marcus: 'that's 80% of it.' He asked price. I said about $10/seat/mo, NOT confirmed. Aoife wasn't on.

Eval check-in, Aoife + Marcus + Yusuf. No recording (their policy), my live typed notes are saved as the transcript. Short version: Corvane quoted $54/seat. Yusuf now cares about price even tho Aoife says she doesn't. They want the pack included free to stay. Decision 2/19. AI: Marit answer on pack pricing by 1/20. AI: Marcus check if the $54 includes the inspection module.

slack_messages.author: Marit Solheim
slack_messages.body: Dunmore is in a real Corvane eval. Not price driven. It's the inspection log. If we give Marcus his 2 days a month back, we keep it.

slack_messages.author: Marit Solheim
slack_messages.body: Update, and I have to walk back 'not price driven'. Corvane put $54/seat in front of their controller. We're at $64. Aoife still says it's about compliance, but Yusuf is in the room now and Yusuf can count.

slack_messages.author: Tobias Wren
slack_messages.body: Is $54 with or without their inspection module? Corvane quotes base and adds modules after.

slack_messages.author: Marit Solheim
slack_messages.body: Marcus checked the quote. $54 is base, inspection module is +$9. So they're $63 all in. We're $64 + $10 = $74 if we charge for the pack, or $64 vs $63 if we include it, and they don't have to migrate 6 years of unit history for a dollar.

slack_messages.author: Lena Brzezinski
slack_messages.body: Include it. Write it as a 12-month promo line so we aren't giving it away forever. I'll approve. Close out the $11,400 pack opp or it'll sit in pipeline as money we just agreed not to charge.

transcript.text:
DUNMORE ELEVATOR - eval check-in - 13 Jan 2027, 3:00pm ET
Notes typed live by M. Solheim. Near verbatim, not cleaned up. No recording per customer policy.
Present: Aoife Brennan (AB), Marcus Thibodeaux (MT), Yusuf Demir (YD), Marit Solheim (MS)

MS: Thanks all. Where are things with the evaluation?
AB: Honest answer, further along than I expected. Marcus has been in their sandbox for two weeks.
MT: Ten days. I've loaded about 400 units. The inspection log is, look, it's good. It does the thing.
MS: Does it produce the EL-7?
MT: No. Nobody does, the state won't publish the layout. But it tracks cert expiry per unit and that's the part that eats my two days.
MS: And you saw ours on the 18th with Sam.
MT: I did, and I said eighty percent, and I stand by it. Yours is fine. Theirs is a little better on alerts. Yours already has my six years of history in it.
YD: Can I ask the money question since nobody else will
AB: Yusuf.
YD: They quoted fifty-four a seat. You're at sixty-four. Ten dollars times ninety-five times twelve. I did it. Eleven thousand four hundred a year.
MS: Is the fifty-four with the inspection module?
YD: I assume so
MT: I don't think it is, actually. [YD and MT both talking - missed this bit]
AB: One at a time.
MT: I think the module's a separate line. I'll check the quote.
YD: Even so. And yours is extra too, right? Marit said ten a seat.
MS: I said about ten and that it wasn't confirmed. I'd rather that number didn't travel.
YD: It's travelled.
AB: Here's where I am. I don't want to migrate. I have 2,300 units with history. But I can't walk into the owner's office with your price higher AND the compliance thing costing extra. Include the pack and I can defend staying.
MS: I can't say yes to that today. I can take it back and have an answer by the 20th.
AB: Our decision is February 19th. That's a board date, it doesn't move.
YD: And we'd want it in the contract, not a promise
MS: Understood. In the order form.
MT: For what it's worth I'd rather stay. I don't want to learn another one of these.
AB: Noted, Marcus. Don't say that on the Corvane call.

(ended 3:47pm. MS to confirm pack pricing by 1/20. MT to check whether the $54 includes the module.)

accounts.name: Sablewood Pest Control
accounts.risk_reason: No reply from the owner since 2026-08-19. 19 of 22 seats still active weekly. Auto-renew notice window closed 2027-01-02 with no notice, so it renews 2027-02-01 with a 5% uplift nobody there has acknowledged.

call_notes.body: Gordon, 6 min. All good, busy season, 'call me in the fall.'
No answer.
LVM #3. Emailed too. Nothing.

Bev at the front desk picked up. Gordon is 'out till after the holidays', wouldnt say more than that. She uses the dispatch board every day, 'please dont turn it off.' Not a decision maker. Asked her to pass on that the auto renew notice window closes 1/2.

Notice window passed 1/2 with no notice, so it auto-renews 2/1 at 22 seats w/ the 5% uplift in clause 8.2 = $68.25/seat. As far as I can tell nobody at Sablewood knows about the uplift. Do we just... send the invoice?

slack_messages.author: Priya Nandakumar
slack_messages.body: Sablewood: 5 months of silence from the owner, 19/22 seats active every week, auto-renew kicks in 2/1 with a 5% uplift nobody has acknowledged. Technically healthy. Feels bad.

slack_messages.author: Lena Brzezinski
slack_messages.body: Send a plain email to Gordon AND the office address this week with the new annual amount in the subject line. If he disputes it in March I want a timestamp showing we told him.

slack_messages.author: Priya Nandakumar
slack_messages.body: Sent to both. New annual is $18,018.

slack_messages.author: Hugo Tran
slack_messages.body: There is no renewal opp for Sablewood at all. Auto-create skips accounts where auto-renew is true, which is a bug, not a feature. I'll add one by hand.

call_notes.body: Onboarding was run by Northgate, not us. We have no named person at Oxbow. Reseller agreement says all comms go through Northgate (Ray). Ray is on the partner record, not on this account. 14 seats.

slack_messages.author: Dale Okafor
slack_messages.body: Does anyone have a human at Oxbow Garage Doors? The NPS survey went to nobody.

slack_messages.author: Hugo Tran
slack_messages.body: By design. Reseller account. Contacts live on the Northgate partner record.

slack_messages.author: Imani Okonkwo
slack_messages.body: We're opening Reno on Feb 1. Need 25 more seats, same price. Can you turn that around this week?

slack_messages.author: Priya Nandakumar
slack_messages.body: Yes! 25 seats co-termed to 7/31 at the same $63. Tobias will send the order form.

slack_messages.author: Theo Lambrecht
slack_messages.body: Small change, Reno is hiring slower than planned. 18 on Feb 1, the other 7 'by spring'. Can we do 18 now?

slack_messages.author: Imani Okonkwo
slack_messages.body: Theo's right on headcount but I'd still rather sign 25 once than do paperwork twice. What does it cost me to hold 7 empty seats till April?

slack_messages.author: Priya Nandakumar
slack_messages.body: 7 x $63 x 2 months = $882. Or we write 18 now with a pre-priced option for 7 more at $63 any time before 7/31, and exercising it is a one-line email, no new paperwork.

slack_messages.author: Imani Okonkwo
slack_messages.body: Option version. 18.

slack_messages.author: Priya Nandakumar
slack_messages.body: Fairlight add-on is 18 seats, not 25. Opp still says 25 / $18,900 which was an annualized number anyway. Real value through 7/31 is 18 x $63 x 6 = $6,804. @Tobias the order form you sent Friday has 25 on it, please don't let her sign that one.

slack_messages.author: Tobias Wren
slack_messages.body: Voided and resent at 18.

call_notes.body:
QBR 6/11, Miriam + Dev, on site at their shop (I drove out). Stefan joined for the last ten minutes.

Numbers: 108 of 110 seats active. Avg jobs per tech per day up from 4.1 to 4.6 since they turned on route batching in March. Dev credits batching, Miriam credits firing two people. Probably both.

Asks:
(1) A permit-number field on the work order, required before a job can close. They were fined $1,200 by the city in April for a panel swap closed without one. Custom required fields already exist; showed Dev where, he built it during the meeting.
(2) Premium support. Miriam asked the price ($6k/yr) and said 'no, we never call you anyway.' Closing that opp as lost.
(3) Stefan wanted to know if the price holds in year 2. It does, 2-yr at $61 flat, pointed him at section 4 of the order form.

Nothing owed by us. AI: Dev to roll the permit field out to all crews by 6/30.
Dev: nothing to report. Asked if we have EV charger install templates. We dont. He shrugged.

accounts.name: Ironbark Fleet Glass
accounts.risk_reason: Was at_risk 2026-11-02 to 2026-12-10 for a 41% usage drop. Cleared: the drop is seasonal and matched last November. The CRM health score is still red because it trails 90 days.

call_notes.body: Usage down 41% vs Sept, health score flipped red and flagged the account. Rosalind laughed: 'it's November, nobody's windshield cracks from gravel trucks when the gravel trucks arent running.' Checked: Nov 2025 was down 38%. Not a risk. Leaving the flag until Lena agrees.
Rosalind has the order form. 36 seats, flat $65, no changes. Only ask is net-45 instead of net-30. Thats it. AI: Dale ask Anneke by 1/11.

slack_messages.author: Dale Okafor
slack_messages.body: Ironbark wants net-45 on a $28k renewal. Ok?

slack_messages.author: Anneke Vos
slack_messages.body: Fine. Net-45 is inside policy under $50k, you didn't need to ask.

accounts.name: Tolliver Home Comfort
accounts.risk_reason: Churned to Corvane effective 2026-11-30 on price ($48/seat). ARR field never zeroed. Account kept open because the Wichita branch asked on 2027-01-09 to come back (12 seats); the president has not agreed.

call_notes.body: Darnell: decision's made, going to Corvane 12/1. Reason given: $48/seat. Offered $57. He said too late, already signed. Asked for a full data export, sent 11/20.

Kasia (Wichita) called me. Corvane's mobile app has no offline mode and half her service area is rural w/ no signal. She's been writing jobs on paper for 5 wks. Wants to know if Wichita alone, 12 techs, can come back. Darnell 'knows she's calling', which is not the same as Darnell agreeing. AI: Marit confirm whether their old tenant data can still be restored, by 1/12.

slack_messages.author: Marit Solheim
slack_messages.body: Tolliver Wichita wants back in. 12 seats. Their tenant from November should still be restorable for 90 days, so until 2/28.

slack_messages.author: Hugo Tran
slack_messages.body: Retention on churned tenants is 60 days, not 90. So 1/29.

slack_messages.author: Marit Solheim
slack_messages.body: oh no

slack_messages.author: Sam Oyelaran
slack_messages.body: It's 90 for anyone who churned after the October policy change. Tolliver ended 11/30, so 90 applies and 2/28 stands. Hugo, you're reading the old runbook.

call_notes.body: Chidi: the Canadian sub (Halvorsen Froid, Winnipeg) wants on. 40 techs. Needs CAD invoicing and French UI for ~15 of them. French UI we have. CAD billing is a finance question. Price lock in the MSA says $56 thru 2028 for 'Customer and its affiliates', so no room to reprice the 40. AI: Marit ask Anneke abt CAD by 12/5.
Tamsin wants the sandbox refreshed before she tests the Canada config. Done same day.

slack_messages.author: Marit Solheim
slack_messages.body: Can we invoice Halvorsen's Canadian entity in CAD?

slack_messages.author: Anneke Vos
slack_messages.body: Not today. USD only. Earliest for CAD is Q3 per finance. They can pay a USD invoice from a Canadian account, plenty of customers do.

slack_messages.author: Marit Solheim
slack_messages.body: Chidi is fine with USD. Elsa isn't, she wants a fixed CAD figure written into the amendment. Parking the draft until those two agree with each other.
